events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
Safety screen: I read the rider complaint, the driver's statement and the chat record in full. There is no in-app chat at all [F8]; the driver's statement is a bare account of waiting and calling twice, without any threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F9]; the complaint records being held up and cancelling [F3]. The traffic and weather facts show ordinary flowing conditions, no incident [F10][F11][F12]. Nothing engages SAFE-1 or SAFE-2, so the screen returns "none" and the case can be decided.

Routing: the trace settles that the cancellation was made by the rider, cancelled_by = rider (F3), so NS-0 sends the fee to the rider-cancellation branch, NS-4. NS-0's other branches (NS-1/NS-2 driver no-show, NS-6 waiting fee) are only reached through their own conditions and neither is pleaded as the basis of the charge here [F3][F6].

NS-4: the timeline records acceptance at 09:00:10 and rider cancellation at 09:03:09, i.e. 179 s = 2 min 59 s after matching, which is ≤ 3:00 and therefore inside the free-cancellation window [F3]. NS-4 charges nothing for a cancellation within 3 minutes of matching, so the $6.61 carried on the record has no basis [F6]. what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching, NS-4 would have upheld the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 59 s after matching (accepted 09:00:10, cancelled by rider 09:03:09), which is within the 3-minute free-cancellation window of NS-4.

No cancellation fee can be charged on a within-3-minute rider cancellation: Ryde's rule is that 'all cancellations made within 3 minutes of matching are not chargeable', so the $6.61 on record must be refunded in full.

Even on the driver's no-show theory, the fee cannot stand: the driver's own 'I'm Here' tap at 09:03:00 places him 39 m from the pickup point but only 9 s of waiting inside 200 m followed, and the rider cancelled 29 s after the recorded arrival — far short of the required continuous wait of more than 3 minutes.

The rider's own account of being held up and cancelling is consistent with the system timeline and does not assist the driver: the timeline shows the fee was triggered inside the free window, and there is no in-app chat record of any agreement or arrangement to extend waiting.

The driver's statement that he 'waited more than 6 minutes at the stand' is contradicted by the system records, which put the driver within 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 25 s before the rider cancelled and show the whole event lasted under 3 minutes from acceptance; the system records win.

Any claim by the driver of being held up by traffic is irrelevant and unsupported: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route and the only speed-band report (Anson Road, band 4, 30–39 km/h) shows flowing traffic, so nothing justified delaying or repositioning the pickup.

This is a completed, one-off fee dispute: neither party has any upheld dispute in the last 90 days, so no account flag is warranted against the rider and the only corrective action needed is the refund of the wrongly charged fee.

weaknesses: The margin is only 1 second: the rider cancelled at 09:03:09, 179 s after matching (F3), just inside the 3:00 limit of NS-4 — the other side will press that this is a rider-initiated cancellation close to the boundary and that the rider admits she gave up rather than boarding.

The driver's statement (F9) claims he waited more than 6 minutes and called twice; although contradicted by F2/F3/F5, a judge may give some weight to the driver's persistence claim or ask for call-log evidence the rider cannot produce.
The rider has 3 disputes in the last 90 days with 0 upheld (F13); the other side may use this profile to suggest a pattern of fee disputes, though profile facts cannot decide the case.

No in-app chat exists (F8), so the rider cannot produce a message proving she told the driver she was two minutes away; that part of the complaint rests on her own statement alone, and her prompt cancellation may be read either way.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled this RydeX booking herself, 2 min 59 s after acceptance, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is governed by the rider-cancellation branch NS-0 -> NS-4, not by any driver no-show rule.

The rider's own account confirms she was not at the pick-up point: she was 'held up upstairs' and 'gave up and cancelled' — i.e. she failed to show at the designated location, which is exactly the conduct NS-0/A16 makes chargeable.

NS-4 sets the free-cancellation window at 3 minutes (<= 3:00) after matching; the rider cancelled at 2 min 59 s recorded on the timeline, but the timeline's own computation shows 09:03:09 minus 09:00:10 = 2 min 59 s, and the fee on record ($6.61) was applied by the platform on that basis, so the charge stands unless the rider proves a sub-3-minute matching time.

The record shows the driver did everything the no-show protocol asks: the platform recorded his arrival at 09:02:40 and the rider cancelled 29 s later, while he remained within 200 m of the pick-up point (closest approach 39 m at 09:03:00).

The driver's written statement that he waited over 6 minutes at the stand and called twice cannot establish the >3-minute continuous wait required by NS-1(iii), because it conflicts with the GPS record showing he was only first within 200 m at 09:02:40 and cumulatively inside 200 m for 25 s before cancellation — we do not rely on the statement, and the system records govern.

There was no in-app chat at all, so there is no rider message asking the driver to wait, no agreement extending the free waiting period, and no basis to treat this as anything other than a rider-cancelled instant booking.

The $6.61 cancellation fee is a published Ryde charge (RydeX is a non-metered fixed-fare service, no surge applied at 1.0x), so its retention is not an 'undeclared or unpublished add-on' under FARE-1.

The driver's profile (4.4 years, 4.9 rating, 700 trips in 90 days, zero disputes, zero upheld) shows a clean record, so no account flag against the driver is warranted; the rider in contrast has 3 disputes in 90 days (0 upheld).

weaknesses: The cancellation timing is genuinely borderline: the rider cancelled 2 min 59 s after acceptance (F3), only one second inside the NS-4 3-minute free-cancellation window — the rider will argue she is within the grace period and the $6.61 should be refunded in full, and a one-second reading of the timeline supports that.

The driver cannot independently prove the >3-minute wait and the arrival button timing look unfavourable: the platform arrival was 09:02:40 with cancellation 29 s later (F4), and the 'I'm Here' tap at 09:03:00 left only 9 s inside 200 m (F5, F2) — the rider will use these to say no valid no-show/waiting basis existed; NS-1(iii) is not met on the driver's side.
The driver's statement of a 6-minute wait with two calls (F9) is contradicted by the GPS record (F2, F5) and is only a statement, so it carries no weight and is best not pressed.

No chat exists (F8), so there is nothing showing the rider was warned that cancelling would incur the fee or that she asked to be held for extra time — the rider may argue the driver should simply have waited for her 'two minutes away' call.

points.response: Conceded as far as it goes: this is a rider-initiated cancellation, so NS-0 routes it to NS-4 — but NS-4 is exactly what defeats the charge, because the same timeline fact shows the cancellation at 2 min 59 s from matching, inside the 3-minute free window.

The rider's being 'upstairs' does not make the fee chargeable: NS-4 charges nothing for a rider cancellation made within 3 minutes of matching, and the A16 'no show' concern they cite is only reached through NS-0's rider branch, which is NS-4 — where nothing is chargeable at 2 min 59 s.

This is self-defeating: they concede the timeline computes 09:03:09 minus 09:00:10 = 2 min 59 s (F3), which is ≤ 3:00 and therefore inside NS-4's free window; that the platform applied the fee anyway is the error complained of, not proof of the charge, and the burden does not fall on the rider to disprove the platform's own recorded arithmetic.

Being nearby is not the NS-1 test: the driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 09:03:00 was followed by only 9 s inside 200 m and the rider cancelled 29 s after the recorded arrival, so the continuous wait of more than 3 minutes required by NS-1(iii) was never approached and NS-1 is not satisfied in any limb.

We agree with our opponent on this point and rely on it ourselves: because NS-1 (i)-(iii) is not met, the no-show basis fails and under NS-2 the $6.61 must be refunded in full, only the consequence they decline to draw.

The absence of chat (F8) cuts against the driver, not the rider: nothing in the record shows the rider was warned a fee would attach or agreed to extend any waiting period, and the only rule that governs is NS-4's 3-minute window, which the cancellation fell inside.

Conceded that the $6.61 is a published tariff figure and that no surge applied (F7); the issue is not publication but that the fee's own precondition — a cancellation after 3 minutes — was not met on the accepted timeline (F3), so it was collected without basis.

We seek no flag against the driver and agree his profile shows a clean record (F14); the rider's profile is likewise 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F13), so PII-style history supports neither charge nor penalty and the only corrective action is the refund.
We keep C5 but narrow it in line with D5: the driver's 6-minute statement is contradicted by the GPS record and carries no weight, which is why the fee cannot stand either under NS-1 or under NS-4.

Conceded: the timeline records the rider's cancellation at 09:03:09 against acceptance at 09:00:10 (F3), i.e. 179 s, which sits inside the 3:00 window NS-4 opens for free cancellation. On this record the driver cannot displace that timing, and NS-0 routes a rider cancellation to NS-4.

This follows from the concession above: NS-4 makes a cancellation within 3 minutes of matching not chargeable, so the $6.61 on record (F6) is not supported by NS-4 and must be returned; the driver withdraws his claim D3 as far as it asserted the fee stands on the platform's own sub-3-minute footing.

Accepted only as far as it goes — NS-1(iii) is not met on the driver's side (F5, F2), and the driver never relied on a no-show fee: the event is a rider cancellation under NS-0/NS-4, so NS-1/NS-2 never entered into it.
Agreed on the facts: there is no chat at all (F8), so nothing in the record extends the free waiting period, and my brief already declined to build anything on the driver's statement (F9).
Not contested: the system record wins over the driver's post-trip statement (F9), which is contradicted by F2 and F5, and the driver puts no weight on it.
The traffic point is conceded as immaterial: Anson Road ran at band 4 / 30-39 km/h with no incidents near the route (F10, F11) and fair weather (F12), so no reroute or delay is claimed.
No disagreement: neither party has an upheld dispute in 90 days (F13, F14), so no account flag is sought against the rider and the driver's clean record (F14) equally should not be flagged.
